FICTIONAL TEST DOCUMENT. Sunrise Textiles versus Global Cotton Suppliers. The buyer contracted for the delivery of five hundred bales of cotton by the end of March. The supplier delivered only two hundred bales, citing floods that blocked the transport routes. The buyer claimed damages for the shortfall, while the supplier relied on the force majeure clause in the agreement. The court held that a force majeure clause excuses performance only when the event makes performance impossible and was beyond the party's control, and mere increase in cost or difficulty does not qualify. On the evidence, the floods closed the only railway route for six weeks, so the supplier was excused for that period but not for the remaining delay. Damages were assessed as the difference between the contract price and the market price on the date of breach, reduced proportionately for the excused period. The decree was modified accordingly and the parties were left to bear their own costs.
